_note: What a card's own texture looks like, measured from the extracted art. 'saturated' is the share of opaque pixels with any real colour; the rest is monochrome line work. The rule of thumb is by card type, not by the 纯色材质 tag: that tag separated the two on four samples and failed on 44.
referenceRule: reference/cards/<type>-<rare>.png, one extracted vanilla card per combination. When present, art.mjs switches to image-to-image so the mode and palette follow a real card instead of a description.
cardFace: 472x1028 RGBA, about half transparent in the shipped cards. The frame, corner ornaments, help button and plate are NOT in this texture; they are drawn by the game.
headIcon: A texture with the same name at 92x92 exists for some cards; extract-art writes it under head/.

plate._note: Read out of the CardShowAssets asset in sharedassets0.assets: the reference order plus each material's _MainTex. Groups of four are the rarities in order stone, copper, silver, gold.

body.note: chars[], items[] and sudans[] are different material objects but all point _MainTex at the same `card` texture, so the body is the same picture tinted per tier.

foreground.sudan: sudan_f, one material for every tier (sudan_forgrond)
foreground._note: This is the per-type difference: a char card has the bottom band and corner brackets, a sudan card has its own frame and its own title font (CardTitle SDF - SudanTitle), an item card has neither.

plate.cardTypeBadge: card_type_char / card_type_item / card_type_sudan at 36x58, plus _required variants, held in the card_type_icons dictionaries

cardBack._note: card.png plus card_d / card_e / card_mt / card_n at 472x1028 are card backs, not bodies. card.png is the back of a gold character card. One copper material uses card_e.

plate.open: what card_d / card_mt / card_n are, and which field uses card_e

emptyAreas._note: Measured on two real stone cards (快脚 2000370, 小圆 2000371), both 472x1028.
emptyAreas.topEmpty: 19.1% and 21.0% of the height is fully transparent: the game writes the card name and a row of small diamonds there.
emptyAreas.bottomEmpty: 2.0% and 2.6%: the art runs almost to the bottom edge, and the frame band is drawn over it.
emptyAreas.rule: Generated art must keep the top fifth blank and may use the bottom. A subject that fills the top hides the card's name.

materialMaps._note: card / card_n / card_d / card_e / card_mt are NOT five different card backs. They are the five texture channels of one PBR material, resolved from each material's texture slots.
materialMaps.consequence: The tiers differ in more than hue: stone is matte (metallic 0.10, gloss 0.40) and silver is shiny (0.85 / 0.80). A flat albedo preview cannot show that, so the page says the preview is albedo only.

sudan._note: Sudan cards use their own frame sudan_f and a cyan, semi-transparent title. Every other tier uses CardTitle SDF - Rare1..4.

stonePlate.answer: stone has NO base-plate image of its own. The body is the one shared `card` paper texture, tinted by the tier material. stone's only per-tier file is stone_f, the frame.
stonePlate.body: card.png — the same mottled paper every tier uses
stonePlate.whyNoStonePng: Because the body was never per-tier. Only the frame and the title font differ per tier.
stonePlate.tintIsNotAMultiply: Multiplying the paper by stone's material _Color #b09aeb produces a purple card; multiplying by the warm #a88864 produces a dark olive one. Neither matches the pale warm grey in game. The face uses a custom shader (CardFaceUnlit, with CardFaceOutline for the rim), plus _DetailAlbedoMap card_d and _MetallicGlossMap card_mt, so the final colour cannot be reproduced with a channel multiply.
stonePlate.consequence: Any offline preview of the tier colour is approximate. Say so, and do not claim the preview is what the game shows.
